claims.claim: Exact harmonic duality gives a polynomial bound on fixed-width boundary signatures.
claims.evidence: For two switching flows x,y with the same supply, summation by parts against the terminal hitting function h_t cancels every nonterminal divergence and gives x^-(t)-y^-(t)=sum_v(d_y(v)-d_x(v))g_t(v). Harmonicity gives g_t(v)=(h_t(s_1(v))-h_t(s_0(v)))/2, so |g_t(v)|<=1/2; since each switching imbalance lies in [0,1], every terminal coordinate has diameter at most N/2. Summing conservation fixes total terminal inflow. If the terminal inflows are integral, the first r-1 coordinates therefore have at most floor(N/2)+1 possibilities apiece, and the last is determined, proving the stated polynomial count for fixed r. For phi identically one, prescribing any imbalance vector d in [0,1]^N leads to an exact linear system for total outflows. Transience of the uniform walk makes the system invertible, and iteration from the all-one vector proves the solution has total outflow at least one, hence nonnegative edge flows. Choosing two imbalance vectors whose difference is sign(g_t) attains sum_v |g_t(v)|.
claims.witness: The exact dual identity, together with the realizable endpoint imbalance vectors d_x(v)=1_{g_t(v)<0} and d_y(v)=1_{g_t(v)>0} for supply phi identically one, is a general extremal certificate.
claims.search_method: Direct derivation from harmonicity, switching-flow conservation, and transience; exact Fraction-arithmetic checks of the identity and extremal construction on the width-three family.

claims.claim: A general range bound survives at arbitrary level width, but it can grow linearly with the number of levels.
claims.evidence: For an edge v->w, shortest-path distance satisfies d(w)>=d(v)-1. Thus a uniform walk starting at level at least i must first hit L_{i-1} before absorption. This hitting time is almost surely finite because the finite binary graph has a sink reachable from every state. The strong Markov property expresses the starting hitting probability as a convex combination of values on L_{i-1}. Consequently m_{i-1}<=m_i<=M_i<=M_{i-1}. Both successors of v in L_i have levels at least i-1 and hence values in [m_{i-1},M_{i-1}], giving |g(v)|=|h(s_0(v))-h(s_1(v))|/2<=W_{i-1}/2. Summing over r vertices per positive level gives the claimed (r/2) sum_i W_{i-1} bound. The family in claim 2 has actual gap mass Theta(k), so linear growth is genuinely possible rather than merely slack in this estimate.
claims.witness: In the k-level width-three family, W_i=1-i/(k+1) and the exact gap mass is k(k+7)/(4(k+1)), which grows linearly in k.
claims.search_method: Strong-Markov first-hit argument plus exact verification of distances, nested ranges, vertexwise gap bounds, and the summed bound in 174 parametric family and padding cases.

claims.claim: For width three, the gap mass and same-supply switching-flow diameter are unbounded; the width-two stability lemma fails already with two positive levels.
claims.evidence: Every constructed vertex has a forward edge and no edge decreases the proposed level by more than one, so the displayed sets are exactly the positive levelsets. Direct substitution gives the unique harmonic values h(a_i)=i/(2(k+1)), h(b_i)=1-i/(2(k+1)), and h(c_i)=1/2. Summing the resulting exact gaps gives k(k+7)/(4(k+1))=Theta(k). Claim 0's realizability argument with common integer supply phi identically one realizes the sign-extreme imbalance vectors, so the sink-inflow diameter equals this mass and is unbounded. At k=2 the listed x and y satisfy nonnegativity, even-minus-odd differences in [0,1], and net outflow one at every nonsink; their sink-1 inflows are exactly 10/3 and 11/6, differing by 3/2>1. Thus the width-two bound fails with only two positive levels. Each padded vertex has value 1/2, and exact summation yields k[4+(r-2)(k+3)]/[4(k+1)] for every fixed r>3.
claims.search_method: Symbolic evaluation of the parametric harmonic solution and mass formula, followed by exact rational checking of 174 family/padding cases, 11 independently solved family systems, 10 extremal flow pairs, and the explicit k=2 certificate.

claims.claim: Within-level hitting-probability order is not locally determined at width three.
claims.evidence: Both completions have exactly L_1={a,b,c} and L_2={X,Y,Z}, are simple binary graphs, and agree on the sinks and all outgoing edges of L_1. Solving the harmonic equations exactly gives (h(a),h(b),h(c))=(3/22,1/22,1/2) in completion A and (1/22,3/22,1/2) in completion B. Hence the order of a and b reverses although the preceding-level order and all current-level outgoing data are identical. This proves failure of local determination of the stated form; it does not assert that no global width-three method exists.
claims.witness: Common edges are a->(0,X), b->(0,Y), c->(0,1), Z->(a,c). Completion A uses X->(c,b), Y->(a,b); completion B uses X->(a,b), Y->(c,a).
claims.search_method: Exact rational solution of both six-variable harmonic systems, together with independent checks of simplicity, distance levels, common local data, and the reversed values.

target_evidence: The exact target asks for a polynomial-time solvability determination for r=3 and ultimately every fixed r>2. Because an ARRIVAL graph's L_0 consists of its two sinks, the draft appropriately interprets width r as applying to positive levelsets; otherwise the target wording would describe an empty class for r>2. The draft proves neither a polynomial-time algorithm nor a contrary complexity classification, and it explicitly acknowledges this. What survives is material but incomplete progress: a polynomial fixed-supply boundary-signature bound and exact counterexamples showing that two essential width-two ingredients—constant switching-flow stability and local level ordering—do not extend to width three. The varying-supply obstacle remains untreated. The final writeup does not claim more, so VALID_PARTIAL_PROGRESS and its claimed PARTIAL resolution are accurate.
